correctness.rationale: Inductive descriptor (color,set of child types) exactly characterizes finite outward-tree bisimilarity, and path-height formulas separate levels. The recurrence counts every realizable nonempty set of at most q types. The binomial estimate for t>=2q and an affine logarithmic recurrence give exp(cq^k)<=t_k<=exp(Cq^k). A logarithmic level split gives universal O(N/log N); independent disjoint subtree colorings realize Omega(N/log N). All boundaries are stated, finite exhaustive tests replayed, and computations are not used as asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: Greatest-bisimulation quotient cardinality measures actual model-state compression, not an arbitrary numerical slice. Uniform complete q-ary trees with only a fixed finite palette form a natural worst-case family. The matching lower bound settles whether the known balanced-tree ordered-DAG rate survives strictly coarser ordinary modal bisimulation; it does, with explicit realizations, a complete rooted-type census and a one-proposition Sylvester specialization.
